editorial.thesis: A mixed-economy city of about 27,000. Its retail is heavy on desserts, sweets & ice cream and banks & atms, and thin on cafés, tea & coffee and grocery & daily needs — and 0% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is about 50% of Ludhiana's. 7.42 chain outlets per lakh residents against 14.79 in Ludhiana; 1 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Baskin Robbins 2.

The mapped economy is close to Ludhiana's mix. Shares of all mapped places: . Raw counts would mislead because Ludhiana is mapped more completely (19,904 places against 29), so we compare mix, not counts.
No large under-served zone. No zone combines a large resident base with retail depth below 60% of the city average; the thin spots are small and scattered.
Retail is less concentrated than in Ludhiana. 14% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Ludhiana 45%). The largest core is Sainik School (9 places).

The widest brand gaps against Ludhiana. Domino's 0 outlets vs 27; Subway 0 outlets vs 20; Café Coffee Day 0 outlets vs 18. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 5 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Ludhiana, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Sainik School is the only mapped zone, with about 6,000 residents. Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 14% of all commercial places, and Sainik School alone lists 9.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Sainik School holds 1 of the 2 tracked chain outlets.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Sainik School has 3 education places and 1 coaching centres.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. There is no large amber area. The blue cores include Sainik School.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (19,904 places in Ludhiana against 29 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Ludhiana; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Ludhiana, Kapurthala's mapped places match the benchmark mix.

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 2 outlets of 1 tracked national brands within 5 km — 7.42 per lakh residents against Ludhiana's 14.79 (223 outlets of 36 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Ludhiana are Domino's (0 vs 27); Subway (0 vs 20); Café Coffee Day (0 vs 18). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Ludhiana's, so low means thin by Ludhiana's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 5 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Kapurthala's age mix against Ludhiana: children (0–14) 21.2% vs 22.0%, 15–24 19.9% vs 19.8%, working age 48.3% vs 48.9%, 60+ 10.6% vs 9.3%. Under-25s are 41% of residents.

zones.144601: A commercial core: 9 mapped places and 1 chain outlets (50% of the city's tracked chains) for about 6,000 residents. A destination zone, so much of its footfall likely lives elsewhere.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 3.5% of mapped places against 4.4% in Ludhiana — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: Haldiram's, Faasos.
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 0.0% of mapped places against 1.7% in Ludhiana — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: Chaayos, Chai Point, Third Wave Coffee.
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 6.9% of mapped places against 0.7% in Ludhiana — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 2 (Ludhiana 7). No mapped outlet in either city: Naturals, Theobroma, Cream Stone.
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 0.0% of mapped places against 2.2% in Ludhiana — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: Big Bazaar, Star Bazaar.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 0.0% of mapped places against 1.1% in Ludhiana — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: MedPlus, Wellness Forever, Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 3.5% of mapped places against 7.4% in Ludhiana — below its share. No mapped outlet in either city: Zudio.
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 10.3% of mapped places against 7.8% in Ludhiana — above its share.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.5% of mapped places against 2.8% in Ludhiana — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 3.5% of mapped places against 4.9% in Ludhiana — below its share.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
